Triggers.value: Other people expressing anger, even calmly

Memory.value: Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it

Negative Appraisals.value: The event happened because of the way I acted
My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe

issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish' directly conflicts with 'I can talk about what happened very easily.' These items describe opposing levels of verbal access to the trauma memory and are hard to reconcile as the same patient's current self-report.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' conflicts with marked memory disturbance items ('some moments are extremely clear while others are completely blank' and 'there are parts of the event I simply cannot remember'). Although fragmented trauma memory can coexist with disclosure, the wording 'very easily' is hard to reconcile with this level of fragmentation in the same profile.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Thought Avoidance: If I think about the event, I will not be able to handle it
issues.explanation: Across Memory and Negative Appraisals, reporting that one can talk about the event 'very easily' sits in tension with the appraisal 'If I think about the event, I will not be able to handle it.' Patients may force themselves to discuss trauma despite distress, but these two statements point in opposite directions and are difficult to integrate clinically without additional context.

vignette: Kaiwai, a 63-year-old Pacific Islander man, still carries the weight of that fateful day when his life was forever altered. It happened during a community event he had organized, where a stage collapse left him trapped under debris, fighting for his life. As he recounts the incident, fragments of memories resurface - the sound of crunching metal, the feeling of suffocation, and the eerie silence that followed. Yet, there are parts of that day that remain shrouded in mystery, lost to the void of his memory. He remembers trying to call out for help but being unable to find the words, as if his voice had been silenced along with his body. As Kaiwai navigates his daily life, he is constantly on guard against triggers that evoke a sense of unease. The sound of raised voices, even in calm discussions, sends his heart racing and transports him back to that moment when everything seemed to fall apart. He avoids confrontations at all costs, often retreating from situations where anger or frustration might be expressed. His community organizing work, once a source of pride and purpose, now feels daunting as he struggles to navigate the complex web of emotions that accompany interactions with others. Kaiwai's encounters with law enforcement or military personnel also leave him feeling unsettled, their uniforms serving as a poignant reminder of the emergency responders who had rushed to his aid. He recalls the feeling of being at the mercy of strangers, unable to control his own fate, and this sense of powerlessness lingers long after the event. As he grapples with these triggers, Kaiwai is haunted by intrusive thoughts that plague him day and night. Memories of the accident resurface unbidden, taunting him with questions about what could have been done differently. He is consumed by self-blame, wondering if his own actions had contributed to the stage collapse. The weight of this guilt settles heavily on his shoulders, leaving him feeling emotionally numb and disconnected from the world around him. Kaiwai's body, too, has become a source of distress, reacting as if still in danger even when he is safe. He startles easily, and his muscles remain tensed, anticipating the next disaster. This hypervigilance exhausts him, making everyday tasks feel like insurmountable challenges. In recent months, Kaiwai's avoidance behaviors have taken a toll on his relationships and work. Colleagues and friends comment on his increased withdrawal, and community events that were once his passion now fill him with dread. His sense of purpose has begun to fray, leaving him feeling lost and uncertain about the future. It was only when Kaiwai realized he could no longer continue living in this state of suspended animation that he finally sought help. As he sits in the therapist's office, he is most afraid of confronting the memories and emotions he has worked so hard to keep at bay. Yet, a glimmer of hope flickers within him - the possibility of finding peace, of rediscovering his sense of purpose, and of learning to live with the scars of that fateful day.
